letter_markdown:
# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Rowan Brooks**
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone] | [Email]

**Date:** [Date this letter is sent]

**To:** Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield — Appeals Department
[Appeal address exactly as printed on my denial letter]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-23**
- **Member:** Rowan Brooks
- **Member ID:** W579327479
- **Reference number:** POC-D47F9A88CC-69885
- **Service denied:** Shoulder labral / instability repair, CPT 29806
- **Plan:** Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield (Commercial/ACA), New Hampshire
- **Governing policy:** *Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Musculoskeletal – Joint Surgery (MSK02-1125.1)*, https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/PDF-Joint-Surgery-2025-11-15.pdf

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of my shoulder labral / instability repair (CPT 29806). The notice dated 2026-08-23 states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking Anthem to reconsider that decision and approve the surgery. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed, and I believe my records meet the plan's own published criteria — including the imaging criterion the denial relied on.

Below I have set out the plan's criteria in its own words and matched each one to what is in my medical records.

---

## The plan's criteria and what my records show

The policy states:

> "Capsulorrhaphy is considered medically necessary when ALL the following criteria are met:"

**1. History of dislocation or recurrent subluxation.** The policy lists:

> "History of a shoulder dislocation or recurrent subluxation"

My records document 12 months of recurrent episodes of shoulder instability with apprehension, and three anterior dislocations since my symptoms began. The most recent dislocation was reduced in the emergency department.

**2. Pain and/or instability interfering with daily activities.** The policy lists:

> "Shoulder pain and/or instability which interferes with age-appropriate activities of daily living"

My records document that I avoid overhead reaching and that I cannot return to work lifting.

**3. Physical exam findings.** The policy lists:

> "Physical exam consistent with symptomatic glenohumeral instability (e.g., apprehension, relocation, load and shift)"

My examination documents a positive apprehension test, a positive relocation test, and increased anterior translation on load-and-shift, with full strength. These are the three exam maneuvers the policy itself names as examples.

**4. Imaging — the reason given for the denial.** The policy states:

> "MRI demonstrates at least ONE of the following:"

and among the findings it lists:

> "A labral lesion consistent with the clinical instability"

My MR arthrogram of the shoulder, performed on 2026-07-29, shows an anteroinferior labral tear (Bankart lesion) with a small Hill-Sachs lesion, glenoid bone loss under 10 percent, and an intact rotator cuff.

An anteroinferior labral tear is a labral lesion, and my instability is anterior — three anterior dislocations, positive apprehension and relocation testing, and increased anterior translation on load-and-shift. The imaging finding and the clinical picture point to the same shoulder, the same direction, and the same diagnosis. That is precisely the correlation the policy asks for. The policy also states:

> "For advanced imaging (CT, MRI, ultrasound, bone scan), there must be a report from a radiologist that correlates with clinical findings. In the absence of such a report, the summary findings from the radiology report should be included in the clinical records."

and:

> "Imaging report. The provider shall submit a detailed imaging report for studies obtained within the past 12 months. In the absence of a detailed report, the provider may submit a report from an independent radiologist."

My study was obtained on 2026-07-29, well within twelve months of the request, and its findings are in my clinical records as summarized above. If the reviewer did not have the full radiology report in front of them, I ask that it be obtained and reviewed before the decision is finalized; I am also asking my surgeon's office to resend it with this appeal. A denial based on imaging should rest on the imaging report itself.

**5. Conservative management.** The policy states:

> "Conservative management1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

and:

> "Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate."

I completed supervised physical therapy focused on rotator cuff and scapular stabilizer strengthening, together with activity modification, from 2026-04-16 to 2026-06-25 — 20 visits over 10 weeks, documented in the physical therapy discharge note. I also took NSAIDs for six months during flares. No injection was given, as it is not indicated for instability. So I completed physical therapy plus additional conservative strategies, and my attendance is documented.

The policy also states:

> "Failure of at least 12 weeks of conservative management (unless history of traumatic dislocation and multiple dislocations during management)*"

and the footnote to that provision states:

> "*For traumatic instability, early surgery may be considered for individuals with large bone defects or individuals under age 35."

My documented physical therapy course ran 10 weeks. I want to be straightforward about that rather than have it come as a surprise on review. The policy's own exception applies to a history of traumatic dislocation with multiple dislocations during management, and my records document three anterior dislocations, the most recent one requiring reduction in the emergency department. I am [age] years old. I ask that Anthem apply its own exception language to my situation and, if it concludes the exception does not apply, that it explain in writing why my three dislocations do not meet it.

**6. No improvement, and more invasive therapy is being considered.** The policy lists:

> "Worsening of or no significant improvement in signs and/or symptoms upon clinical reevaluation"

and:

> "More invasive forms of therapy are being considered"

and:

> "Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care"

After 20 physical therapy visits and six months of NSAIDs, I continued to have instability and apprehension, I dislocated again, and my examination remains positive for instability. My shoulder did not improve with conservative care, and surgery is the next step my surgeon has recommended.

---

## One request about the criteria themselves

Several of the provisions I have quoted end with a colon and introduce lists that I was not able to reproduce in full here. The policy lists further conditions that I have not set out. If Anthem is relying on any criterion I have not addressed, I ask that the plan identify in writing the specific criterion it applied and the specific documentation it found missing, so that my surgeon and I can respond to it directly.

---

## Closing request

I am asking Anthem to overturn the denial dated 2026-08-23 and authorize CPT 29806. My records document a history of dislocation, functional limitation, a physical exam consistent with glenohumeral instability, an MR arthrogram showing a labral lesion that matches that instability, and a completed course of physical therapy plus additional conservative measures that did not help.

My denial notice states that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of that notice, by 2027-02-19. I am sending this letter to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, and I will follow up using the contact information Anthem has provided to me.

Please send me a written decision, and please include the specific criteria and records relied upon. If this appeal is not approved, please tell me what further levels of appeal are available to me, including any independent external review.

I am glad to provide anything else that would help, and my surgeon's office can be reached to supply additional records or to speak with the reviewing physician.

Thank you for taking another look at my case.

Sincerely,

**Rowan Brooks**
Member ID: W579327479
[Signature]
[Date]

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-23 (Reference POC-D47F9A88CC-69885)
- MR arthrogram report dated 2026-07-29
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-16 to 2026-06-25, 20 visits)
- Office notes from Dr. Marchetti, MD, orthopedic surgery
- Emergency department record of shoulder reduction
- [Any other records you wish to include]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
